reunion_a.text: The tunnel narrows to a single track's width. On the platform, in matching raincoats and under a flickering light, stand two men who very much look as though they have been asked to wait in a corridor.
Ah. You again. We've been asked to hold the Northern line.
Hold it is a strong word. We've been asked to stand on it. Shall we get this over with?
Splendid. We hold the Northern line. I shall say you were terrifying.
I shall say it was a draw. And that the wind was against us. Underground. It's a technicality.
We were never here, of course. We were at the golf club.
They saunter off towards the exit, arguing amiably about which of them will tell Vane. The tunnel clears.

reunion_b.text: Down a long dim passage, two women sit side by side on a bench under a map of the Tube, each holding a paper cup. They stand up as one.
We both handed in our lanyards. Vane sent them back. With a fruit basket.
We're here because it's in our contracts. We're not here to win. But we won't make it easy.
That's us done. Properly, this time. It was good to see you in the end. I've missed the daylight, actually.
I'm for the first train to Glencoe, and my wellies. Tell Vane, if you must, that I've decided I'd rather be wet than right.
They walk away together up the tunnel, already comparing which of them has the worse commute. The way is clear.

ug_station_guard.text: Please keep behind the yellow line. Please keep behind the yellow line. Please keep behind... oh. Hello. You're in the wrong tunnel. Everyone is.
There are 272 stations on the Tube. Some people try to visit them all in a day. It's called the Tube Challenge, and it's one of those things that sounds bad but is secretly delightful.

ug_cleaner.text: The mice here are famous. They ride the escalators. I've seen one with a ticket. Clearly an annual pass.
Rumour is something big lives in the old tunnels. Every time I look, it's just a mole in a hi-vis jacket. I'm choosing to believe it's a mole.
